comparison_limits: S ordinary and W axis demonstrate a nonzero terminal scorer gradient under their own runs, not that W ordinary should have a nonzero gradient on every batch.
The saved W axis and S ordinary/axis batch name orders match for all three attempts. The failed W ordinary details/names were never written, so their actual equality is not independently established.
Old F.output.1.weight primary-hinge versus weighted-auxiliary diagnostics do not measure pool_score.weight, omit primary CE and other parameters, and do not prove the cause of this failure.
An auxiliary weight ratio of 1/50 does not establish a particular gradient ratio or a numerical-underflow cause.

findings.title: RGB scorer remains connected to the actual F auxiliary objective
findings.detail: The second F pool scores first-main11 normalized [B,7,512] PF directions, pools them, and feeds frequency_neck/classifier plus the original feature triplet. For RGB W, the objective is .001*(.25*label-smoothed CE + 1.0*softTriplet). W overwrites parent weights and P reads the updated anchor; no stale .05 reset or duplicate weight multiplication was found.
findings.implication: Source does not justify requires_grad=False, deleting the scorer, or treating the failure as an unconnected parameter.

findings.title: The scorer has no main11 or partial task-loss rescue path
findings.detail: Main11 uses router relation/band/psi scores and per-relation PF; it does not call frequency_expert.pool_score. The controlled pools and controlled01 band score use this scorer, but calibrator context is detached and O targets run under no_grad. Partial forward returns before the auxiliary pools. Hence this scorer receives task-loss gradient through the scored F auxiliary path only, while PF/output weights also have the main loss/value paths.
findings.implication: Nonzero direct PF gradients can coexist with zero scorer gradients. Changing the auxiliary coefficient is relevant context but is not a complete causal diagnosis.

findings.title: Ordinary frequency pooling is not algebraically forced to be useless
findings.detail: frequency_shared selects structured=False. It expands the shared candidate values across three source groups, but each group uses query[band]+source[group]. Conditional cross-band reads and relation/band routing can further differ. Those operations do not force all seven projected PF unit directions to be identical. Actual relation dispersion is not logged.
findings.implication: A finite-precision collapse or small directional variance is possible but unmeasured. The previous MS T mean/freeze rescue cannot be copied as proof that this RGB scorer is obsolete.

findings.title: FP32 pooled output does not certify FP32 scoring/backward
findings.detail: PF directions are captured and normalized in FP32, but the second scored pool calls its Linear and softmax outside a local autocast-disabled block, inside G full forward autocast. Existing feature_dtype reports the pooled FP32 result, not the scorer output, softmax, upstream gradient or backward dtype. Native scaler starts at512; actual W ordinary scaler history is absent.
findings.implication: The scorer precision boundary is a specific place to instrument. Neither AMP underflow nor cancellation is established by source alone.

findings.title: The existing gate examines only the terminal update gradient
findings.detail: Each step zeroes gradients, and the runner tests p.grad only after accumulating three successful optimizer updates. The Boolean merges None, nonfinite and exact-zero L1; neither parameter-level values nor prior update history are written before the assertion. Reaching line111 also proves the earlier direct-PF finite/nonzero assertions did not fail. This is not evidence that the scorer was inactive throughout all three updates.
findings.implication: The terminal check is stronger than graph connectivity alone, but no evidence yet justifies declaring this agreed protocol inappropriate. Preserve its original failure and unchanged acceptance requirements.

findings.title: MS T mean and frozen scorer status do not apply to RGB
findings.detail: Only MS selects T, which replaces both actual-loss score pools with means and therefore freezes exactly1024 obsolete score parameters. RGB selects unchanged S scored pools with both scorers trainable. RGB total99585158/trainable1887366 matches both current native metadata and the old S ordinary/axis records.
findings.implication: There is no current parameter-count blocker or missing MS frozen-parameter exception to fix, and no reason to edit the active MS code.

mathematical_local_check.formula: For z_j, a_j=softmax(w^T z_j), u=sum_j a_j z_j and g=dL/du, dL/dw=sum_j a_j*(g^T(z_j-u))*z_j; batch reduction applies.
mathematical_local_check.scope: Exact-arithmetic local score-pool Jacobian, with coefficient already included in g; derived from current score-pool source, not a measured tensor result.
mathematical_local_check.interpretation: Identical z_j, a locally orthogonal upstream gradient, cancellation, or finite-precision operations may produce a zero score gradient while the direct value/PF gradient remains nonzero. The saved evidence does not identify which occurred.

minimal_next_action.recommendation: One separately source-reviewed, isolated RGB ordinary diagnostic replay before selecting any training fix.
minimal_next_action.scope: New RGB-only diagnostic entry/output; same original teacher, seed42, fresh heads and Adam, P8K8, .001, native AMP/scaler512, unchanged full/partial forward and two-backward path. Up to the original three successful-update native gate; keep original all-gradient/strict-reload requirements and truthful exit.
measurements: Record each attempt and actual optimizer update, scaler before/after, batch names, pool-score requires_grad, and separate None/finite/nnz/min/max/L1/L2 values for the actual scorer gradient before unscale and after unscale/step; persist before the unchanged final assertion.

Capture first-main11 PF unit directions and their cross-relation differences, second-F-pool logits/softmax/output dtypes and ranges, and the real auxiliary upstream gradient to the pooled PF. Identify only the second F pool; the controlled first pool and controlled01 scorer are different calls.

On the same captured z, score weights and upstream gradient, compare the native local score-pool VJP with a detached diagnostic-only FP32 local recomputation. Use the current scaler consistently and record scaled/unscaled values. This checks the pool Jacobian, not an alternate full-model loss.

If the combined gradient cancels, retain same-forward weighted CE and softTriplet gradient contributions separately to distinguish objective cancellation from a disconnected path. Do not re-run extra neck/model forwards or update from diagnostic branches.
Keep diagnostic autograd.grad/hook events separate from the actual scaled backward; existing S/M autograd probes must not be mistaken for real accumulated p.grad or change it.
minimal_next_action.failure_preservation: If the unchanged terminal gate fails, write diagnostic evidence first and keep nonzero exit; do not produce SMOKE_PASS or start formal RGB.
minimal_next_action.no_reproduction_rule: A non-reproduction is a diagnostic result, not proof of the original cause or permission for seed/scale searches.
